searchDocs.title: EZUtil
searchDocs.content: EZUtil EZUtil is a collection of small, game-agnostic Roblox utilities. Every module is exposed as a field of the package root and is required lazily, the first time that field is read, so a client-only module never runs on the server (and the reverse). local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local EZUtil = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.EZUtil) print(EZUtil.TableUtil.tableLength({ a = 1, b = 2 })) -- 2 print(EZUtil.MathUtil.shortenNumber(1200)) -- 1.2K print(EZUtil.DateUtil.formatDuration(3725)) -- 1h 2m 5s -- Modules can also be required on their own. local TableUtil = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.EZUtil.TableUtil) The package root is fully typed, so EZUtil. autocompletes every module and its functions. Modules [AimIndicator]: a neon disc that marks where an ability will land. [CharacterRigUtil]: humanoids, animators, body parts and skinned mesh rigs. [DateUtil]: timestamps, periods and human-readable durations. [FixedRewardSequence]: deterministic, evenly spread reward sequences. [GroundUtil]: downward ground projection and one-call raycasts. [InstanceUtil]: tag lookups, welds and look-at tweens. [JanitorUtil]: safe Janitor destruction. [LayoutUtil]: ScrollingFrame canvas and item sizing. [MathUtil]: rounding, formatting, random values and positions. [ParticleUtil]: particle templates, bursts and cleanup. [PlayerUtil]: humanoids, animations, group ranks and player UI. [ProfileUtil]: named MicroProfiler scopes. [ProjectileUtil]: ballistic projectiles and aim preview beams. [SearchUtil]: searching Instance trees and nested tables. [SystemUtil]: timers, connections, product info and platform checks. [TableDiffUtil]: shallow table comparison. [TableUtil]: table and string helpers. [VfxUtil]: attribute-driven VFX templates.

searchDocs.title: build​
searchDocs.content: </> FixedRewardSequence.build( weights: {number}-- Positive weights, one per reward. Errors if empty or if any weight is not positive. ) → {number}-- A frozen array of indices into weights. Builds a frozen cycle of reward indices whose counts are proportional toweights. The cycle has at least 100 entries (more when the rarest weight is under 1% of the total), its counts are allocated by largest remainder, its entries are interleaved as evenly as possible, and it starts at the first occurrence of the rarest reward. A single weight returns { 1 }.

searchDocs.title: dateTimeComponentsToTimestamp​
searchDocs.content: </> DateUtil.dateTimeComponentsToTimestamp(components: DateTimeComponents) → number Converts UTC date and time components to a unix timestamp in seconds. The milliseconds are kept as a fraction. DateUtil.dateTimeComponentsToTimestamp({ Year = 2024, Month = 1, Day = 1, Hour = 0, Minute = 0, Second = 0, Millisecond = 0, }) -- 1704067200

searchDocs.title: unix​
searchDocs.content: </> DateUtil.unix() → number Get the current unix timestamp in UTC time. This is the number of seconds since January 1, 1970.

searchDocs.title: getPeriod​
searchDocs.content: </> DateUtil.getPeriod( timestamp: number, duration: number,-- The period length in seconds. Must be greater than zero. offset: number?-- Shifts where periods start, in seconds. Defaults to 0. ) → number Returns the index of the fixed-length period that contains timestamp, counting from the unix epoch shifted by offset. Useful for daily or weekly resets: two timestamps are in the same period when this returns the same number. local today = DateUtil.getPeriod(DateUtil.unix(), DateUtil.SECONDS_PER_DAY) -- Days that reset at 12:00 UTC instead of midnight local shiftedDay = DateUtil.getPeriod(DateUtil.unix(), DateUtil.SECONDS_PER_DAY, 12 * 3600)

searchDocs.title: getPeriodEnd​
searchDocs.content: </> DateUtil.getPeriodEnd( period: number,-- A period index from DateUtil.getPeriod. duration: number,-- The period length in seconds. Must be greater than zero. offset: number?-- Defaults to 0. ) → number Returns the timestamp at which period ends (and the next one starts). Use the same duration and offset that were passed to DateUtil.getPeriod. local today = DateUtil.getPeriod(DateUtil.unix(), DateUtil.SECONDS_PER_DAY) local secondsUntilReset = DateUtil.getPeriodEnd(today, DateUtil.SECONDS_PER_DAY) - DateUtil.unix()

searchDocs.title: formatDuration​
searchDocs.content: </> DateUtil.formatDuration(seconds: number) → string Formats a duration as hours, minutes and seconds. Negative durations are treated as 0 and fractions of a second are dropped. DateUtil.formatDuration(3725) -- "1h 2m 5s" DateUtil.formatDuration(59) -- "0h 0m 59s"

searchDocs.title: formatUnix​
searchDocs.content: </> DateUtil.formatUnix( timestamp: number,-- Rounded down to a whole second. format: string,-- The DateTime format string to use. locale: string?-- The locale to use. Defaults to en-us. ) → string-- The formatted time in local time. Formats a unix timestamp in local time with aDateTime format string. Example local secondsLeft: number = 80 DateUtil.formatUnix(secondsLeft, "mm:ss") -- 01:20 DateUtil.formatUnix(DateUtil.unix(), "YYYY-MM-DD") -- today's date

searchDocs.title: timeAgo​
searchDocs.content: </> DateUtil.timeAgo( timestamp: number, endTimestamp: number?-- The timestamp to compare to. Defaults to the current time. ) → string Describes how long ago timestamp was, listing every non-zero unit from years down to seconds. Returns "now" for less than a second. Months and years are averages (30.44 and 365.24 days). Example DateUtil.timeAgo(DateUtil.unix() - 80) -- "1 minute 20 seconds ago" DateUtil.timeAgo(100, 160) -- "1 minute ago" DateUtil.timeAgo(100, 100) -- "now"

searchDocs.title: totalTime​
searchDocs.content: </> DateUtil.totalTime( timestamp: number, endTimestamp: number?,-- The timestamp to compare to. Defaults to the current time. separator: string?,-- The separator to use between each unit. Defaults to a space. depth: number?-- The maximum number of units to return. ) → string Like DateUtil.timeAgo, but without the "ago" suffix, with a custom separator and an optional limit on how many units are listed. Returns "now" for less than a second. Example DateUtil.totalTime(0, 3725) -- "1 hour 2 minutes 5 seconds" DateUtil.totalTime(0, 3725, ", ") -- "1 hour, 2 minutes, 5 seconds" DateUtil.totalTime(0, 3725, " ", 2) -- "1 hour 2 minutes"

searchDocs.title: scope​
searchDocs.content: </> ProfileUtil.scope( label: string,-- The name shown in the MicroProfiler. callback: () → T...-- A function that does not yield. ) → T...-- The values returned by callback. Runs callback inside a MicroProfiler scope named label and returns whatever it returns. The scope is always closed, and an error thrown by callback is re-raised after it closes. Only use this for synchronous code: callback must not yield. local path = ProfileUtil.scope("ComputePath", function() return computePath(start, goal) end)

searchDocs.title: resolveUDim​

searchDocs.title: FixScrollingCanvas​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> LayoutUtil.FixScrollingCanvas( layout: UIGridStyleLayout ,-- The UIListLayout or UIGridLayout inside the frame. scrollingFrame: ScrollingFrame , padding: UIPadding? -- Padding to add around the content. ) → () → ()-- Stops updating the canvas. Turns off AutomaticCanvasSize and keeps CanvasSize fitted to the layout's content plus any padding, never smaller than the visible window. Only the axes the frame scrolls on are sized; the other axis is set to 0. Updates are batched to the next Heartbeat after a child is added or removed, the content or window size changes, the scrolling direction changes, or the padding changes.

searchDocs.title: FixAuthoredListHeights​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> LayoutUtil.FixAuthoredListHeights( scrollingFrame: ScrollingFrame , layout: UIListLayout , items: {GuiObject }-- The list items, whose current Size.Y is kept. ) → () → ()-- Disconnects and destroys the size constraints. The layout's padding is not restored. Locks each item and the layout's padding to the height they were authored with, resolved against the scrolling frame's visible height. Scale heights then stay relative to the viewport instead of growing with the canvas. Each item gets a UISizeConstraint, and the layout's Padding is rewritten in pixels whenever the window resizes.

searchDocs.title: FixLayout​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> LayoutUtil.FixLayout( layout: UIGridStyleLayout , scrollingFrame: ScrollingFrame , itemAspectRatio: (number | UDim2 )?, padding: UIPadding? ) → () → ()-- Disconnects and destroys the constraints this call created. Adds a UIAspectRatioConstraint to each visible item in the scrolling frame and keeps the vertical canvas fitted to the content plus any top and bottom padding. Items added later are constrained as they arrive. Items that already have a UIAspectRatioConstraint of their own are left alone. itemAspectRatio decides the ratio: a positive number is used for every item; a UDim2 is converted to a ratio once, against the frame's canvas size minus padding; any other number (0, negative or infinite) gives each item the ratio of its own Size against the frame's size, re-applied whenever the frame resizes; nil adds no constraints and only fixes the canvas.

searchDocs.title: shortenNumber​
searchDocs.content: </> MathUtil.shortenNumber( number: number | string, minimumTiers: number?-- The minimum number of tiers to shorten. Defaults to 1. ) → string Shortens a large number to a readable format. Useful for displaying large numbers that don't require exact precision. Common use cases are for displaying XP, money in leaderboards, damage etc. Shortened numbers keep one decimal place, truncated rather than rounded, so a value never reads as more than it is: 999,999 shortens to 999.9K instead of rolling up to 1,000K. Example: MathUtil.shortenNumber(1000) -- 1K MathUtil.shortenNumber(1200) -- 1.2K MathUtil.shortenNumber(999999) -- 999.9K MathUtil.shortenNumber(1000000) -- 1M MathUtil.shortenNumber(1000000000) -- 1B MathUtil.shortenNumber(1000000000000) -- 1T MathUtil.shortenNumber(1000000000000000) -- 1Q minimumTiers is useful for when you want to shorten a number but only if it's at least a certain tier. For example, to only shorten numbers of 1,000,000 or more: MathUtil.shortenNumber(250000, 2) -- 250,000 MathUtil.shortenNumber(1000000, 2) -- 1M A tier is the amount of commas in a number. For example, 1,000,000 has 2 tiers and 1,000 has 1 tier. Tier list and their abbreviations: 1,000 = K 1,000,000 = M 1,000,000,000 = B 1,000,000,000,000 = T 1,000,000,000,000,000 = Q

searchDocs.title: getUserLevel​
searchDocs.content: This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> PlayerUtil.getUserLevel(player: Player ) → number Gets a player's permission level, one of the PlayerUtil.userLevel values: creator if PlayerUtil.isCreator is true; in a group-owned game: superuser for rank 253 and above, moderator for rank 99 exactly, and VIP for ranks below 10 (including players outside the group); otherwise premium for Premium members, or normal. Example: PlayerUtil.getUserLevel(player) -- 0

searchDocs.title: getHumanoid​

Example: PlayerUtil.getHumanoid(player) -- Humanoid PlayerUtil.getHumanoid(workspace.Zombie) -- Humanoid

searchDocs.title: getCharacterHeight​

searchDocs.title: isAlive​

Example: PlayerUtil.isAlive(player) -- true PlayerUtil.isAlive(workspace.Zombie) -- false PlayerUtil.isAlive(workspace.Part) -- false

Gets the Player whose character contains a BasePart, by walking up its ancestors until one holds a Humanoid. Also available as PlayerUtil.getPlayerFromPart. Example: hitbox.Touched:Connect(function(part) local player = PlayerUtil.getPlayerFromInstance(part) end)

searchDocs.title: disableOtherUi​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> PlayerUtil.disableOtherUi( value: boolean,-- true to hide, false to restore. exception: string?-- The name of a ScreenGui to leave alone. ) → () Hides or restores every ScreenGui in the local player's PlayerGui, except the one named exception and any whose name contains "Topbar". Hiding remembers each ScreenGui's Enabled state so restoring puts it back. PlayerUtil.disableOtherUi(true, "ShopGui") -- hide everything but the shop PlayerUtil.disableOtherUi(false) -- restore

searchDocs.title: ProjectileConfig​
searchDocs.content: </> interface ProjectileConfig { part: BasePart -- The part to move. It is anchored for the flight. origin: Vector3 -- Where the flight starts. target: Vector3 -- Where the arc lands after duration seconds. duration: number-- Flight time in seconds. faceDirection: boolean?-- Point the part along its velocity. Defaults to false. gravity: Vector3? -- Defaults to workspace.Gravity, pointing down. raycastParams: RaycastParams?-- When set, each frame's movement is raycast to detect hits. maxBounces: number?-- How many times to bounce off hit surfaces before stopping. Defaults to 0. bounceDamping: number?-- Velocity multiplier applied on each bounce. Defaults to 0.7. onHit: (( position: Vector3 , normal: Vector3? ) → ())?-- Called once when the flight ends. normal is nil when it ends by reaching the end of the arc. onBounce: (( position: Vector3 , normal: Vector3 , bouncesLeft: number ) → ())?-- Called after each bounce. } Options for ProjectileUtil.launch.

searchDocs.title: ProjectileController​
searchDocs.content: </> interface ProjectileController { Cancel: (self: ProjectileController) → ()-- Stops the flight where it is, without calling onHit. IsActive: (self: ProjectileController) → boolean-- Whether the projectile is still flying. } Returned by ProjectileUtil.launch.

searchDocs.title: AimBeamConfig​
searchDocs.content: </> interface AimBeamConfig { origin: Vector3 -- Where the arc starts. target: Vector3 -- Where the arc lands. duration: number-- Flight time in seconds, which sets how high the arc goes. gravity: Vector3? -- Defaults to workspace.Gravity, pointing down. parent: Instance -- Where to put the beam's holder part. color: Color3? -- Defaults to white. width: number?-- Defaults to 0.5. transparency: NumberSequence? -- Defaults to 0.5. } Options for ProjectileUtil.createAimBeam.

searchDocs.title: AimBeam​
searchDocs.content: </> interface AimBeam { Update: ( self: AimBeam, origin: Vector3 , target: Vector3 , duration: number ) → ()-- Redraws the arc. Destroy: (self: AimBeam) → ()-- Destroys the beam and its holder part. } Returned by ProjectileUtil.createAimBeam.

searchDocs.title: calculateLaunchVelocity​
searchDocs.content: </> ProjectileUtil.calculateLaunchVelocity( origin: Vector3 , target: Vector3 , duration: number,-- Flight time in seconds. gravity: Vector3? -- Defaults to workspace.Gravity, pointing down. ) → Vector3  Returns the initial velocity that carries a projectile from origin to target in exactly duration seconds under gravity.

searchDocs.title: getPositionAtTime​
searchDocs.content: </> ProjectileUtil.getPositionAtTime( origin: Vector3 , velocity: Vector3 ,-- The launch velocity. time: number,-- Seconds since launch. gravity: Vector3? -- Defaults to workspace.Gravity, pointing down. ) → Vector3  Returns the projectile's position time seconds after launch.

searchDocs.title: getVelocityAtTime​
searchDocs.content: </> ProjectileUtil.getVelocityAtTime( velocity: Vector3 ,-- The launch velocity. time: number,-- Seconds since launch. gravity: Vector3? -- Defaults to workspace.Gravity, pointing down. ) → Vector3  Returns the projectile's velocity time seconds after launch.

searchDocs.title: launch​
searchDocs.content: </> ProjectileUtil.launch(config: ProjectileConfig) → ProjectileController Anchors config.part and moves it along the ballistic arc from config.origin to config.target every Heartbeat. Without raycastParams the part flies the full arc and onHit is called with the final position and a nil normal. With raycastParams, each frame's movement is raycast: on a hit the part either bounces (reflecting its velocity, scaled by bounceDamping, while bounces remain) or stops and calls onHit with the hit position and surface normal.

searchDocs.title: createAimBeam​
searchDocs.content: </> ProjectileUtil.createAimBeam(config: AimBeamConfig) → AimBeam Draws the ballistic arc from config.origin to config.target with a single curved Beam, held by an invisible, anchored, non-colliding part parented to config.parent. Call Update to redraw it as the aim changes. local beam = ProjectileUtil.createAimBeam({ origin = hand.Position, target = mouseHit, duration = 0.8, parent = workspace, }) RunService.RenderStepped:Connect(function() beam:Update(hand.Position, mouseHit, 0.8) end)

searchDocs.title: timeout​
searchDocs.content: </> SystemUtil.timeout( delay: number,-- Seconds to wait. callback: (number) → ()-- Receives the seconds elapsed since the timeout started. ) → () Calls callback once at least delay seconds have passed, checking every RunService.Stepped. Does not yield. Example: SystemUtil.timeout(1, function() print("One second later") end)

searchDocs.title: interval​
searchDocs.content: </> SystemUtil.interval( interval: number,-- Seconds between calls. callback: ( number, number ) → boolean?-- Receives the seconds elapsed since the interval started and the last frame's delta time. ) → RBXScriptConnection  Calls callback every interval seconds, checking every RunService.Stepped. Each call runs in its own thread. Return false from the callback, or call :Disconnect() on the returned connection, to stop the interval. Example: local ticks = 0 SystemUtil.interval(1, function() ticks += 1 return ticks < 10 -- stop after 10 ticks end)

searchDocs.title: inTable​
searchDocs.content: </> SystemUtil.inTable( searchTable: {[any]: any}, target: any ) → boolean Checks if a value is in a table. Example: SystemUtil.inTable({ 1, 2, 3 }, 2) -- true SystemUtil.inTable({ 1, 2, 3 }, 4) -- false SystemUtil.inTable({ Part, 2, 3, Part2 = true }, Part) -- true

searchDocs.title: disconnect​
searchDocs.content: </> SystemUtil.disconnect(connection: RBXScriptConnection? | {RBXScriptConnection? }) → () Disconnects a connection, or every connection in an array. Nil values and non-connections in the array are skipped. SystemUtil.disconnect(connection) SystemUtil.disconnect({ connectionA, connectionB })

searchDocs.title: getProductInfo​
searchDocs.content: This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> SystemUtil.getProductInfo( productId: number, infoType: Enum.InfoType?-- Defaults to Enum.InfoType.Asset. ) → {[any]: any}? Returns MarketplaceService:GetProductInfo for a product. Successful results are cached for the lifetime of the server or client, and failed requests return nil instead of erroring. local info = SystemUtil.getProductInfo(productId, Enum.InfoType.Product) if info then print(info.Name, info.PriceInRobux) end

searchDocs.title: isMobile​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> SystemUtil.isMobile() → boolean Returns whether the player is on a touch device: touch is enabled and neither a keyboard nor a mouse is. In Studio only TouchEnabled is checked, so the device emulator counts as mobile.

searchDocs.title: isConsole​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> SystemUtil.isConsole() → boolean Returns whether a gamepad is enabled. This is also true on PC or mobile while a controller is connected.

searchDocs.title: uprightAt​
searchDocs.content: </> VfxUtil.uprightAt( template: BasePart , position: Vector3 ) → CFrame  Returns a CFrame at position that keeps the template's own rotation.

searchDocs.title: play​
searchDocs.content: </> VfxUtil.play( template: BasePart , cframe: CFrame , parent: Instance? -- Defaults to workspace. ) → BasePart -- The playing clone. Plays a one-shot copy of template at cframe. The clone and every part inside it are anchored and made non-colliding, each ParticleEmitter is played according to its attributes, Lights fade to zero brightness over 0.35 seconds, and the clone is destroyed once its longest emitter has finished. VfxUtil.play(effects.Slam, VfxUtil.uprightAt(effects.Slam, hitPosition))

searchDocs.title: attach​
searchDocs.content: </> VfxUtil.attach( template: BasePart , part: BasePart -- The part to weld the effect to. ) → () → ()-- Stops the effect and cleans it up. Welds a copy of template to part and enables all of its emitters, returning the stop function. Stopping switches the emitters and lights off, which lets the particles already in flight fade out on their own before the clone is cleaned up. Calling the stop function more than once does nothing. local stop = VfxUtil.attach(effects.Aura, character.HumanoidRootPart) task.wait(5) stop()

searchDocs.title: getPartCount​
searchDocs.content: </> SearchUtil.getPartCount(instance: Instance? ) → number Counts the BaseParts among the descendants of the given instance. Warns and returns 0 if instance is nil. Example: SearchUtil.getPartCount(workspace.NPC) -- 5

searchDocs.title: getDescendantParts​
searchDocs.content: </> SearchUtil.getDescendantParts(instance: Instance ) → {BasePart } Gets all parts in the given instance Example: SearchUtil.getDescendantParts(game.Workspace.LightPost) -- { [1] = Light, [2] = PostMeshPart }

searchDocs.title: getAncestor​
searchDocs.content: </> SearchUtil.getAncestor( child: Instance , condition: string | (obj: Instance ) → boolean ) → Instance?  Walks up from child, starting with child itself, and returns the first instance that matches condition. A string matches by name; a function matches when it returns true. Returns nil if nothing matches. Example 1: local map = SearchUtil.getAncestor(part, "Map") Example 2: detector.Touched:Connect(function(part: BasePart) local bot: Model? = SearchUtil.getAncestor(part, function(instance: Instance) return instance:HasTag("NPC") end) if bot ~= nil then print("NPC bot touched the detector") end end)

searchDocs.title: find​
searchDocs.content: </> SearchUtil.find( node: Instance | {[any]: any}, condition: any | (obj: any) → boolean,-- A predicate, or a key to look for. maxDepth: number?,-- How many levels to search. Defaults to 1. _depth: number?-- Internal: tracks the current depth. Leave as nil. ) → any Searches the children of node (an Instance's children, or a table's values) level by level and returns the first match. The search continues until maxDepth is reached, a match is found, or there is nothing left to search. Returns nil when no match is found. By default maxDepth is 1, so only the direct children of node are searched. condition can be: a function, called with each child; the first child it returns true for is returned; a key, checked on each child: for Instance children, the child's own child with that name is returned; for table children, the table that has that key is returned. Function condition example: local player: Player? = SearchUtil.find(game.Players, function(player: Player) return player.Name == "Player1" end) Key example: -- The first Humanoid inside a direct child of workspace local humanoid = SearchUtil.find(workspace, "Humanoid") Table example: local NPCs = { { Name = "NPC1", Health = 0 }, { Name = "NPC2", Health = 20 }, { Name = "NPC3", Health = 0 }, } local firstAliveNPC = SearchUtil.find(NPCs, function(NPC) return NPC.Health > 0 end) -- { Name = "NPC2", Health = 20 }

searchDocs.title: exists​
searchDocs.content: </> SearchUtil.exists( node: Instance | {[string]: any}, children: (string | {string})? ) → boolean Checks if the given node has children (for an Instance) or keys (for a table) with the given names. A single name can be passed as a string, or several names as a table. Returns false if children is nil. Instance node example: SearchUtil.exists( character, { "Head", "UpperTorso", "LeftUpperArm", "RightUpperArm" } ) -- true SearchUtil.exists(character, "Head") -- true Table node example: local config = { Damage = 10, Range = 20 } SearchUtil.exists(config, { "Damage", "Range" }) -- true SearchUtil.exists(config, "Cooldown") -- false

searchDocs.title: getFirstPart​
searchDocs.content: </> SearchUtil.getFirstPart(instance: Instance? ) → BasePart?  Returns the first BasePart among the direct children of the given instance. Example: SearchUtil.getFirstPart(workspace.Player1) -- Head

searchDocs.title: flip​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.flip( source: {[any]: any},-- The table you want to flip mergeDuplicates: boolean?-- Merge key duplicates into a table instead of overwriting them. ) → {[any]: any} Flips the table's keys with its values. If mergeDuplicates is true, All values will be stored in a table at the key's index, instead of overwriting them. Example: TableUtil.flip({ a = 1, b = 2 }) -- { [1] = "a", [2] = "b" } TableUtil.flip({ a = 1, b = 2 }, true) -- { [1] = { "a" }, [2] = { "b" } } -- Use case: finding all keys with the same value local newTable = TableUtil.flip({ a = 1, b = 2, c = 2 }, true) -- { [1] = { "a" }, [2] = { "b", "c" } } print(#newTable[2]) -- 2

searchDocs.title: map​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.map( source: {[any]: any},-- The table you want to map callbackFn: ( any, any, any ) → ( any, any )-- The function to map the table with ) → {[any]: any} Maps a table or instance to a new table. Example: TableUtil.map({ 1, 2, 3 }, function(v) return v * 2 end) -- { 2, 4, 6 } TableUtil.map({ 1, 2, 3 }, function(v, i) return i * 2 end) -- { 2, 4, 6 }

searchDocs.title: filter​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.filter( source: {[any]: any} | Instance ,-- The table you want to filter callbackFn: ( any, any, any ) → (boolean?)-- The function to filter the table with (element, index, source). Keeps elements it returns exactly true for. ) → {any} Filters a table, or an Instance's children, into a new array. Example: local noTwo = TableUtil.filter({ 1, 2, 3 }, function(value) return value ~= 2 end) -- { 1, 3 } local parts = TableUtil.filter(workspace, function(value) return value:IsA("Part") end) -- { Part, Part2 }

searchDocs.title: mapIndex​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.mapIndex( source: {any},-- The array you want to map filterFn: (( value: any, index: number, source: {any} ) → ( any?, any? ))?-- Returns the new value and, optionally, the new key ) → {[any]: any} Maps an array to a new table. The callback can return a new value, and optionally a new key to store it under; otherwise each value keeps its position. Example: TableUtil.mapIndex({ 1, 2, 3 }) -- { [1] = 1, [2] = 2, [3] = 3 } TableUtil.mapIndex({ 1, 2, 3 }, function(v) return v * 2 end) -- { [1] = 2, [2] = 4, [3] = 6 } TableUtil.mapIndex({ "a", "b" }, function(v, i) return i, v end) -- { a = 1, b = 2 }

searchDocs.title: trimWhitespace​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.trimWhitespace(text: string) → string Trims leading and trailing whitespace from a string. Example: TableUtil.trimWhitespace(" Hello, world! ") -- "Hello, world!"

searchDocs.title: trimLeadingWhitespace​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.trimLeadingWhitespace(text: string) → string Trims leading whitespace from a string. Example: TableUtil.trimLeadingWhitespace(" Hello, world!") -- "Hello, world!"

searchDocs.title: trimTrailingWhitespace​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.trimTrailingWhitespace(text: string) → string Trims trailing whitespace from a string. Example: TableUtil.trimTrailingWhitespace("Hello, world! ") -- "Hello, world!"

searchDocs.title: split​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.split( text: string | number?, delimiter: string?, trimTrailingDelimiter: boolean?, trim: boolean?-- Trim whitespace from each chunk ) → {string} Splits a string into a table of strings using a delimiter. If delimiter is not provided, it defaults to a space. Setting trimTrailingDelimiter to false will result in an empty string at the end of the table if the text ends with the delimiter Setting trim to false will result in whitespace not being trimmed from each chunk Example: TableUtil.split("Hello, world!") -- { "Hello,", "world!" } TableUtil.split("Hello, world!", ", ") -- { "Hello", "world!" } TableUtil.split("Hello, world!", ",", nil, false) -- { "Hello", " world!" } -- no whitespace is trimmed TableUtil.split("Hello, world!,", ",", false) -- { "Hello", "world!", "" } -- trailing delimiter is included TableUtil.split("path/to/file", "/") -- { "path", "to", "file" } TableUtil.split("path/to/file/", "/") -- { "path", "to", "file" } -- trailing delimiter is trimmed

searchDocs.title: join​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.join( stringTable: {[any]: string | number},-- The table you want to join separator: string?-- The separator to use when joining the table. Defaults to ",". ) → string Joins an array of strings and numbers into a single string, with separator between each element. Example: TableUtil.join({ "Hello", "world!" }, ",") -- "Hello,world!" TableUtil.join({ "Hello", "world!" }, ", ") -- "Hello, world!"

searchDocs.title: extend​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.extend( arg1: boolean | {[any]: any},-- The target table, or true for deep mode arg2: {[any]: any},-- The first table to merge in, or the target table in deep mode ...: {[any]: any}-- The tables you want to merge into the target table ) → {[any]: any} Extends a table with one or more tables, in order, and returns it. The target table is modified in place. Example: TableUtil.extend({ a = 1 }, { b = 2 }, { c = 3 }) -- { a = 1, b = 2, c = 3 } TableUtil.extend({ a = 1 }, { a = 2 }, { a = 3 }) -- { a = 3 } -- Last argument overwrites previous arguments TableUtil.extend({ a = 1 }, { a = 2 }, { a = 3 }, true) -- Error: Argument #3 must be a table Config override example: local function getDefaultConfig() return { health = 100 } end local buffConfig = { health = 150, speed = 1.5 } local playerConfig: { [any]: any } = TableUtil.extend(getDefaultConfig(), buffConfig) -- { health = 150, speed = 1.5 } Pass true as the first argument for deep mode, in which case the target table is the second argument. Note that nested tables are currently assigned by reference rather than merged key by key.

searchDocs.title: assign​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.assign( targetTable: {[any]: any},-- The target table you want to assign values to ...: {[any]: any}-- The tables you want to merge into the target table ) → {[any]: any} The assign function copies all properties from one or more source objects to a target object. Alias for TableUtil.extend.

searchDocs.title: treePath​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.treePath( tree: {[any]: any} | Instance ,-- The table or instance you want to get the value from path: string,-- The path to the value delimiter: string?-- The delimiter to use when splitting the path ) → any Gets a value from a table or Instance using a path. Example: TableUtil.treePath({ a = { b = { c = 1 } } }, "a.b.c") -- 1 TableUtil.treePath({ a = { b = { c = 1 } } }, "a.b") -- { c = 1 } TableUtil.treePath(game.Workspace, "House.Door") -- Door instance TableUtil.treePath(script, "NonexistantChild") -- nil

searchDocs.title: insertIf​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.insertIf( target: {[any]: any},-- The table you want to insert the value into value: any,-- The value you want to insert condition: nil | boolean | () → boolean?-- The test condition ) → nil Inserts a value into a table if the test condition is true. Example: TableUtil.insertIf({ 1, 2, 3 }, 4, true) -- { 1, 2, 3, 4 } TableUtil.insertIf({ 1, 2, 3 }, 4, false) -- { 1, 2, 3 } TableUtil.insertIf({ 1, 2, 3 }, 4, function() return true end) -- { 1, 2, 3, 4 }

searchDocs.title: instanceChildrenToTable​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.instanceChildrenToTable( instance: Instance -- The instance you want to collect children from ) → {[string]: Instance } Collects all children of an instance into a table. Example: TableUtil.instanceChildrenToTable(game.Workspace) -- { Part = Instance, Part2 = Instance } TableUtil.instanceChildrenToTable(game.ReplicatedStorage.Config) -- { Config1 = CFrameValue, Config2 = StringValue }

searchDocs.title: tableLength​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.tableLength(source: {[any]: any}) → number Returns the total amount of values in a table. Example: TableUtil.tableLength({ 1, 2, 3 }) -- 3 TableUtil.tableLength({ a = 1, b = 2, c = 3 }) -- 3

searchDocs.title: tableRandomIndex​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.tableRandomIndex( obj: {[any]: any} | Instance -- The table or instance you want to get a random index from ) → any Returns a random index from a table or instance. Example: TableUtil.tableRandomIndex({ 1, 2, 3 }) -- 2 TableUtil.tableRandomIndex({ a = 1, b = 2, c = 3 }) -- "b"

searchDocs.title: indexOf​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.indexOf( obj: {[any]: any}, value: any ) → any Returns the key of the first value equal to value, or 0 if there is none. TableUtil.indexOf({ "a", "b", "c" }, "b") -- 2 TableUtil.indexOf({ "a", "b", "c" }, "z") -- 0

searchDocs.title: tableRandom​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.tableRandom( obj: {[any]: any} | Instance -- The table or Instance to select from. ) → any-- nil if the table is empty. Returns a random value from a table, or a random child of an Instance. TableUtil.tableRandom({ "a", "b", "c" }) -- "b" TableUtil.tableRandom({ x = 1, y = 2 }) -- 2

searchDocs.title: makeConfigFromValues​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.makeConfigFromValues( folder: Folder | Configuration -- The folder or Configuration you want to make a table from ) → {[string]: any} Creates a nested table of value instances from a Folder or Configuration instance. Example: Config (Folder) -- in ReplicatedStorage Origin (CFrameValue), Value = CFrame.new(0, 1, 0) WelcomeMessage (StringValue), Value = "Hello, world!" TableUtil.makeConfigFromValues(game.ReplicatedStorage.Config) Result: { Origin = CFrame.new(0, 1, 0), WelcomeMessage = "Hello, world!" }

searchDocs.title: tableRemove​
searchDocs.content: </> TableUtil.tableRemove( obj: {any},-- The array you want to remove elements from removeTest: number | {any}-- The index to remove, or a list of values to remove ) → nil Removes elements from an array in place, shifting the remaining elements down. Example: local list = { "a", "b", "c" } TableUtil.tableRemove(list, 2) -- list is now { "a", "c" } local values = { 1, 2, 3, 2 } TableUtil.tableRemove(values, { 2 }) -- values is now { 1, 3 }
